planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic soil in partial to full shade, siting it where the darkened stems and leaf undersides can be viewed against a light backdrop.

directions: Plant in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, the same demanding conditions required by the straight species. 'Chocolate' is a foliage-focused selection prized for its dark, purplish-bronze young stems and leaf petioles, which contrast handsomely with the plant's large, palmate green leaves through the growing season before the typical pale-yellow, waxy bells appear in late summer. Because the color effect is most visible on new growth, cutting back tired stems in early summer can encourage a fresh flush of the darker coloration. Keep soil consistently moist and never allow the root zone to dry out, as with all kirengeshoma.

common_name: Cherry Ingram Cappadocian Navelwort (Large-Flowered Intense-Blue Selection)

planting.note: Divide established clumps or plant container-grown stock in spring or early fall into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade; this selection is a heavier bloomer than the species type.

directions: Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled to full shade. 'Cherry Ingram' is a long-favored named selection of Cappadocian navelwort valued for producing an especially heavy flush of larger, more saturated sky-blue flowers with a crisp white eye than the species average, held in loose sprays above mounded, heart-shaped foliage in early to mid spring. It stays neatly evergreen through the season in mild climates and slowly spreads by creeping rhizomes into an attractive groundcover patch. Pair it with hellebores, epimediums, and early ferns, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor and flower quality.

common_name: Lingholm Himalayan Blue Poppy (Fertile Perennial Blue-Flowered Selection)

planting.note: Sow fresh seed in fall or cold-stratify and start indoors in late winter into acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil; unlike many blue poppies, 'Lingholm' sets viable seed and comes true enough from seed to be propagated this way.

directions: Plant in cool, moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in part shade, ideally in a climate with mild, humid summers. 'Lingholm' is the most widely distributed and garden-worthy clone from the Meconopsis x sheldonii/Fertile Blue Group, selected for combining the large, luminous sky-blue flowers of the Himalayan poppy with a genuinely perennial, non-monocarpic habit and reliable seed-set, making it far more forgiving for home gardeners than straight M. betonicifolia. Remove any flower buds that form in the plant's first year to channel energy into building a strong root system before allowing it to bloom. It performs best where summers stay cool and humid, struggling badly with heat and drought, and benefits from a thick summer mulch to keep roots cool and moist.

common_name: Allenii Wood Anemone (Large Lavender-Blue Historic Selection)

planting.note: Plant dormant rhizomes or divisions in fall into moist, humus-rich woodland soil in dappled shade; 'Allenii' is a vigorous, larger-flowered heirloom selection dating to the late 1800s.

directions: Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained woodland soil in dappled to full spring shade. 'Allenii' is one of the oldest named wood anemone selections still in commerce, prized for its comparatively large, star-shaped flowers in a rich lavender-blue with a slightly darker reverse to the petals, held above the typical deeply cut, ferny foliage in early to mid spring. Like the species, it goes fully dormant by early summer, so interplant it with later-emerging ferns or hostas to fill the space it leaves behind. Established colonies spread gradually by rhizome and are best left largely undisturbed, divided only every several years right after foliage yellows if increase is desired.
